source: prolonged exposure to nicotine, by weakening this response

source: prolonged exposure to nicotine, by weakening this response, decreased aversion to the drug

source: prolonged exposure to nicotine, by weakening this response, decreased aversion to the drug, and hence boosted consumption

claim: Mice titrate their nicotine dose in the two-bottle choice experiment.
source: resulting in titration of the nicotine dose, as previously reported

source: We classified these mice (17/35) as 'avoiders'

source: Overall, only a small proportion of the mice (7/35, all non-avoiders) reached a plateau in their consumption

claim: Avoiders and non-avoiders showed similar nicotine intake for low concentrations of nicotine (10 and 50 µg/ml).
source: Avoiders and non-avoiders (phenotypes defined as above throughout the manuscript) showed on average similar nicotine intake for low concentrations of nicotine (10 and 50 µg/ml, p>0.05)

claim: Nicotine intake increased throughout the task for non-avoiders, reaching 16.9±2.9 mg/kg/day for 200 μg/ml of nicotine.

source: Aversion to nicotine in avoider mice mainly occurred at the transition from 100 to 200 μg/ml

source: but some mice displayed aversion at concentrations as low as 10 μg/ml

source: Together, these results show that most mice can actively track or avoid nicotine, indicating that they can discriminate nicotine from the control solution
